name: io.crela/mcp
title: Crela
description: Search the Crela software marketplace and publish, update and review your software from your agent.

tools.name: search_software
tools.description: Search the Crela marketplace for reviewed software, apps and games you buy once and own - no subscription. Returns only approved, publicly listed tools, each with a url to its Crela page where it can be bought. Use limit (1-50) to keep the response small and page through the rest; get_software returns the full detail of one.

query.description: Full-text search over title and description

lang.description: Language of the software user interface, e.g. "de". Not the programming language.

page.description: 1-based page, see total_pages in the response

tools.name: get_software
tools.description: Full public detail of one approved software item by its slug: description, price, platforms, version, system requirements and the url of its Crela page.

slug.description: The software slug from search_software, e.g. "knowledge-editor"

tools.name: get_submission_requirements
tools.description: Return the machine-readable submission rules for selling software on Crela (required fields, KO rules, bundle rules). Public, no sign-in required. Use it to check whether a project fits Crela before building. Uploading builds, screenshots and clips (precheck_build, submit_new_software, update_software, upload_screenshot and upload_clip) needs files from disk and is only available in the local server (npx -y @crela/mcp). This server manages existing software: list_my_software, check_review_status, get_review_report, set_metadata.

tools.name: list_my_software
tools.description: List all software you own with its id, slug, review status (pending/approved/rejected/flagged), whether it is unlisted, price and sales count. Use this to recover the software_id needed by check_review_status, set_metadata and delete_software. Unlike search_software, this also returns pending, rejected and unlisted tools. Requires sign-in to your Crela account; your client asks you to connect when you first use it.

tools.name: get_my_software_details
tools.description: Read the full metadata and media list of one of your own software items by software_id. Works for all statuses (pending, approved, rejected). Returns { tool, media, missing_media, presentation } where media lists all uploaded screenshots/images with their ids and sizes, and presentation attests the listing level (incomplete, minimum, ideal) with toward_ideal, the steps left to the ideal presentation. Use this to verify current state after set_metadata, to get media ids before calling delete_media, or to read current metadata before an update. Requires sign-in to your Crela account; your client asks you to connect when you first use it.

tools.name: check_review_status
tools.description: Poll the lightweight review status of a submitted software (progress, sub-step, rate-limit budget). Returns { tool_id, tool_status, awaiting_media, missing_media, presentation, next_step, version, review_job_status, review_sub_step, review_passed, rejection_reason, review_started_at, review_completed_at, rate_limit }. awaiting_media true means the tool is approved but not listed yet because screenshots are missing (missing_media). Polling: poll every 30 s until review_job_status is neither "queued" nor "running"; a full review takes 5-15 minutes. If review_passed is false after completion: call get_review_report for structured findings. rate_limit.updates_remaining_today shows the budget shared by set_metadata and new builds. Requires sign-in to your Crela account; your client asks you to connect when you first use it.

tools.name: get_review_report
tools.description: Fetch the full review report of a submitted software: pass/fail, rejection reasons and structured findings to fix. Heavier than check_review_status - call this only after the review has completed, not for live progress polling. Findings are capped at 10 locations each (a CVE finding can carry hundreds of near-identical ones); the response then sets truncated:true and locations_omitted per finding. Raise max_locations_per_finding when you actually need the long tail. Requires sign-in to your Crela account; your client asks you to connect when you first use it.

max_locations_per_finding.description: How many locations to keep per finding, default 10

tools.name: set_metadata
tools.description: Change metadata (title, description, price, categories, tags, etc.) of an existing software - no binary upload. On an approved tool, a new title, description or long_description gets a quick automatic text check: it goes live at once, or the response has text_check with outcome "review" and a reason: the check objected, the change waits for a full review in which a person at Crela decides, and the current text stays until then (change the text and send it again for a new check). Changing categories or age_rating (on a game also a change to age_rating_source, age_rating_reasons or age_rating_questionnaire), or upgrading price_eur from 0 to a paid value, triggers a re-review; text changed in the same update waits for it. All other fields (tags, price reductions, tool_languages, unlisted) do NOT trigger re-review. Set unlisted:true to take an approved tool off the market (reversible with unlisted:false) - existing buyers keep access, it just cannot be newly purchased. Rate limit: 5 updates per tool per 24 h (shared with new builds). check_review_status shows your remaining budget. Requires sign-in to your Crela account; your client asks you to connect when you first use it.

price_eur.description: 0 for free, or at least €0.50 (the smallest amount our payment provider can charge)

sale_price_eur.description: Discounted price (at least €0.50 (the smallest amount our payment provider can charge) and below price_eur); null ends the sale. Buyers see the lowest price of the 30 days before the sale crossed out

sale_ends_at.description: ISO timestamp when the sale ends; null = open-ended

trial_enabled.description: Enable a time-limited trial for a paid tool

license.description: Leave it unset unless the license changes. An empty string means the Crela Standard EULA. An open source license (SPDX identifier, e.g. MIT, Apache-2.0, GPL-3.0-only) can be set or changed here when the builds of the tool already carry it: the license text as LICENSE or COPYING and, for copyleft licenses, the source archive in crela-source/. Copyleft tools can only be free. If a build lacks them, the call fails and names the version: ship a version with these files via update_software, wait for its approval, then set the license. It takes effect at once, without a new review, and a free tool then runs without license enforcement.

drm_mode.description: Paid tools are forced to sdk_required server-side regardless of this

framework.description: Usually auto-detected from the build; override only if wrong

tool_languages.description: ISO 639-1 codes of every language the software user interface is available in, e.g. ["en","de"]; replaces the whole list. NOT the programming language.

platforms.description: Correct the platforms when the ZIP auto-detection got them wrong

privacy_policy.description: Privacy policy text; null clears it. KO_09 rejects a build whose code contacts an analytics or telemetry service that this text does not name.

support_contact.description: Support contact shown to buyers, e.g. an email address; null clears it

security_updates_until.description: Date until which you provide security updates (YYYY-MM-DD), not in the past; from 11 December 2027 at least two years from today; five years recommended. Shown to buyers before they buy. Can be changed but not removed

safety_notes.description: Warnings and safety information buyers need, e.g. flashing lights or changes to system settings (plain text, max 2000 characters); null clears it

network_mode.description: Network allowlist mode: "none" = the app needs no network, "declared" = it only talks to the hosts in network_hosts, "user_chosen" = the user picks the servers. null clears it. Applies from the next build.

network_hosts.description: Hosts your app connects to, e.g. ["api.example.com", "*.cdn.example.com"]. Every host that receives user or device data must also be named in privacy_policy (KO_09). Applies from the next build.

video_url.description: https YouTube/Vimeo link; null removes the video entry

unlisted.description: true = take off market (hidden, not purchasable); false = re-list

age_rating.description: Every product needs an age rating before it is listed (Australian online safety codes; German JMStV for games). Games must send it with the submission and when their category changes to game. Send together with age_rating_source, age_rating_reasons and age_rating_questionnaire. Ratings are 0, 6, 12, 16 or 18; from 6 name the reasons. If the game already has a USK rating, use it: an own assessment must not be lower. A person at Crela checks every game before it is listed.

age_rating_source.description: Where the age rating comes from: self (your own assessment), usk, pegi or iarc

age_rating_reasons.description: Reasons for the age rating, e.g. "fantasy violence without blood"; required from 6

age_rating_questionnaire.description: Every product: answer every content question truthfully (true = the software contains it). For games any true answer rules out age rating 0; for software that is not a game, contact and purchases are shown as information and do not.

violence.description: Fighting or violence, including cartoon or fantasy violence

fear.description: Scary or threatening scenes, horror or a frightening atmosphere

language.description: Crude language, insults or discriminating content

drugs.description: Alcohol, tobacco or drugs shown or mentioned

gambling.description: Gambling, simulated gambling or loot boxes

contact.description: Users can chat with or contact other users

purchases.description: Purchases inside the software or game

tools.name: delete_software
tools.description: Permanently and irreversibly delete one of your software items. Only works if it has never been sold - sold tools cannot be deleted (buyers keep their claim); take those off the market with set_metadata { unlisted: true } instead. Requires sign-in to your Crela account; your client asks you to connect when you first use it.

tools.name: delete_media
tools.description: Permanently delete a screenshot, logo or other media item from a software listing. Use get_my_software_details to get the media ids of uploaded files. Uploaded files (screenshots and logos) are also deleted from storage; video URL entries are only removed from the listing. Requires sign-in to your Crela account; your client asks you to connect when you first use it.

media_id.description: The id of the media item (from get_my_software_details response)

tools.name: update_media
tools.description: Update a media item: the sort order of any item (lower sort_order appears first), or the URL of a video entry (https YouTube/Vimeo link only). This tool does not create entries: a video is added with set_metadata { video_url }. Use get_my_software_details to get media ids. Provide at least one of sort_order/url. Requires sign-in to your Crela account; your client asks you to connect when you first use it.

media_id.description: The id of the media item (from get_my_software_details response)

sort_order.description: Display position; lower values appear first

url.description: New video URL (video entries only; https YouTube/Vimeo)

tools.name: get_sdk_marker
tools.description: Fetch the per-tool SDK marker (KO-10) of an EXISTING tool by software_id. Embed it via the build env var CRELA_SDK_MARKER before building a new version. For a tool that does not exist yet use preview_marker (needs slug, not software_id). Requires sign-in to your Crela account; your client asks you to connect when you first use it.

tools.name: preview_marker
tools.description: Compute the per-tool SDK marker (KO-10) for a NOT-yet-created tool from its planned slug. Paid tools (price > 0) must embed this marker via the build env var CRELA_SDK_MARKER before building and submitting. For tools that already exist use get_sdk_marker (needs software_id, not slug). Returns { marker, slug, slug_available }. Requires sign-in to your Crela account; your client asks you to connect when you first use it.

slug.description: The planned URL slug of the tool you are about to submit

tools.name: get_product_page
tools.description: Read the product page of one of your software items as set_product_page writes it: blocks (what visitors see), pending_blocks (your text changes waiting for review), media (every upload with id, type, size and where it appears), unplaced (screenshots in no block; they still show in the media stage at the top), hero (the clip at the top of the page), cover (the image on cards and launcher tiles), presentation (listing level with toward_ideal) and warnings (dead media ids, missing description block, no clip). Read it before set_product_page to get the media ids, and again afterwards to check that warnings is empty. Requires sign-in to your Crela account; your client asks you to connect when you first use it.

If the check is unavailable, the text waits (the response has changes_pending_review) and is checked again automatically. Images, clip, video and layout go live at once. Read get_product_page afterwards: warnings should be empty. Requires sign-in to your Crela account; your client asks you to connect when you first use it. blocks.description: The whole page, top to bottom; replaces the current blocks. Schema in the tool description.

tools.name: set_cover
tools.description: Choose one of your uploaded screenshots as the cover: the 16:9 image on website cards and launcher tiles. Without a chosen cover the first screenshot is used. Landscape, at least 1280 x 720 px. zoom (1 to 3) and focal_x/focal_y (0 to 1, the point that stays in view) set the crop; media_id null resets to the first screenshot. Get media ids from get_product_page. Requires sign-in to your Crela account; your client asks you to connect when you first use it.

media_id.description: Id of an uploaded screenshot, or null to reset

focal_x.description: Horizontal point that stays in view, 0 (left) to 1 (right), default 0.5

focal_y.description: Vertical point that stays in view, 0 (top) to 1 (bottom), default 0.5
